title: Geriatric oncology, AYA and cancer in pregnancy

steps.tx: **Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment** CGA evaluates functional status, comorbidities, cognition, nutritional state, polypharmacy, and social support, identifying hidden **vulnerabilities** missed by routine ECOG performance status. Multi-domain CGA scoring unmasks frailty and physiological vulnerability, guiding tailored antineoplastic dose attenuations and targeted supportive interventions to prevent treatment-related institutionalisation.

steps.tx: The **G8 screening** questionnaire is a validated 8-item tool where scores of 14 or less indicate **impaired functional reserve** warranting in-depth comprehensive geriatric evaluation. The G8 survey assesses appetite changes, weight loss, mobility, neuropsychological problems, body mass index, polypharmacy, and self-perceived health status relative to age-matched peers.

left.title: CARG Toxicity Score (0 to 23 Points)
points: Low risk (0-5 pts): 24% risk of grade 3-5 toxicity
Medium risk (6-9 pts): 52% risk of grade 3-5 toxicity
High risk (10-23 pts): 83% risk of grade 3-5 toxicity
Guides proactive dose reductions and growth factor support

right.title: CRASH Score (Chemotherapy Risk Assessment)
points: Stratifies risk into haematological and non-haematological toxicity
Haematological predictors: lymphocytes, IADL, LDH, diastolic BP
Non-haematological predictors: ECOG, cognition, MNA nutrition
Predicts severe toxicity independent of standard Karnofsky index

steps.tx: The Cancer and Aging Research Group **CARG toxicity score** predicts severe grade 3 to 5 **chemotherapy-related toxicities** in older adults based on clinical and laboratory parameters. Developed across diverse malignant tumours, the CARG predictive model integrates age, tumour type, planned chemotherapy dosing intensity, creatinine clearance, haemoglobin, and patient-reported fall history.

left.title: Paediatric-Inspired AYA Protocols (e.g. CALGB 10403)
points: Substantially higher cumulative doses of PEG-asparaginase
Intensive weekly vincristine and high-dose dexamethasone pulses
Aggressive intrathecal CNS prophylaxis without cranial irradiation
3-year event-free survival 66% to 78% in young adults

right.title: Historical Adult ALL Protocols (e.g. Hyper-CVAD)
points: Heavy reliance on cyclical anthracyclines and cyclophosphamide
Lower cumulative asparaginase exposure due to adult toxicity fears
Higher myelosuppression and infectious treatment-related mortality
Event-free survival historically under 40% to 50% in AYA group

steps.tx: **Adolescent and young adult** **AYA oncology** addresses distinct biological entities, clinical trial underrepresentation, and unique survivorship, fertility, and psychosocial needs in patients aged 15 to 39 years. Tumour biology in AYAs frequently displays distinct driver pathways compared to paediatric or older adult counterparts, mandating tailored clinical trials and dedicated survivorship care.

nodes.label: New Cancer Diagnosis in Reproductive-Age Patient
Male: Sperm Banking Prior to Any Cytotoxic Dose
Prompt Initiation of Systemic Anticancer Therapy

edges: Add letrozole if estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer
Zero oncological delay to curative treatment

steps.tx: Adolescents and young adults, usually defined as aged **15 to 39 years**, do better on **paediatric-inspired regimens** for acute lymphoblastic leukaemia than on adult-type regimens. Fitness, organ function and risk features still guide intensity. Fertility should be discussed at diagnosis, and sperm banking should not delay induction chemotherapy. Early referral to a specialist AYA service supports safe delivery.

steps.tx: **Fertility preservation** counseling is mandatory prior to initiating gonadotoxic chemotherapy, offering sperm **cryopreservation** for postpubertal males and oocyte or embryo **cryopreservation** for females. Controlled ovarian hyperstimulation using random-start antagonist protocols with letrozole allows rapid oocyte retrieval within two weeks without causing treatment delays in hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer.

rows: Goserelin 3.6 mg SC Q4W starting >= 1 week before chemo
Ovarian failure rate reduced from 22% to 8% (OR 0.30, p=0.04)
Significantly higher pregnancy rate with goserelin (21% vs 11%)
Long-term ovarian function preservation confirmed (72% vs 64%)
Safe and effective across HR-negative and HR-positive breast
Does not compromise disease-free or overall survival

steps.tx: The diagram traces **fertility preservation** before gonadotoxic chemotherapy through **ovarian stimulation** with gonadotropins, ultrasound guided transvaginal oocyte retrieval, and rapid **vitrification** of oocytes or embryos in liquid nitrogen. Acting before treatment matters because alkylating drugs can cause lasting ovarian failure, while this planned sequence secures future reproductive options without delaying cancer care.
steps.say: This diagram shows the oncofertility workflow for a young female patient before gonadotoxic chemotherapy. Random start ovarian stimulation grows multiple follicles, then transvaginal ultrasound guided retrieval collects oocytes, followed by ultra rapid freezing of oocytes or embryos. Counseling about this path before treatment preserves future fertility and allows cancer therapy to start on time.

vis.alt: The diagram shows ovarian stimulation followed by transvaginal oocyte retrieval and embryo freezing in nitrogen.
vis.caption: Oncofertility workflow preserves oocytes before gonadotoxic treatment. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: GnRH agonists **goserelin** or **leuprolide** administered during adjuvant chemotherapy significantly reduce **premature ovarian insufficiency** and improve subsequent pregnancy rates in young breast cancer patients. In the randomized POEMS and PROMISE-GIM6 trials, concurrent GnRH analogue administration reduced post-chemotherapy ovarian failure by more than 50% without compromising disease-free survival.

rows: Major structural organ malformations (up to 20%), spontaneous miscarriage
Low teratogenic risk; monitor for intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR)
Low structural risk; monitor fetal growth, amniotic fluid volume, and Doppler
Avoid delivery during maternal or neonatal neutropenic nadir

steps.tx: **Chemotherapy in pregnancy** can be safely administered starting in the **second trimester** after organogenesis is complete, whereas methotrexate and radiotherapy are strictly contraindicated during pregnancy. Doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, and paclitaxel can be safely given during the second and third trimesters, but therapy must stop by week 35 to 37 to avoid perinatal neonatal neutropenia.

left.title: Contraindicated in Pregnancy
points: Methotrexate: severe craniofacial, skeletal, CNS malformations
Trastuzumab: profound oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, renal failure
Tamoxifen: Goldenhar syndrome, ambiguous genitalia, fetal demise
Immune checkpoint inhibitors: high rate of immune-mediated spontaneous abortion

right.title: Permissible in 2nd / 3rd Trimester
points: Doxorubicin / Epirubicin: extensive placental clearance, safe cardiac profile
Cyclophosphamide: standard component of FAC/AC regimens
Paclitaxel: acceptable if clinically indicated for breast cancer
Platinum agents (Cisplatin/Carboplatin): permissible for advanced cervical/ovarian

steps.tx: Physiological **pharmacokinetic changes** in pregnancy including expanded plasma volume and enhanced renal clearance alter chemotherapy distribution and clearance, but standard dosing based on **actual body weight** is recommended. Despite higher hepatic blood flow and increased volume of distribution, empiric dose reductions lead to inferior maternal survival; dosing based on actual pregnant weight ensures adequate oncological cure.
